title: BUILD-NRT-054-pnpm-roster-conflicts-read-only-script
universal_lens: Roster truth is modeled as a constrained optimization over a directed acyclic graph of evidence nodes. The read-only conflict script computes the maximum likelihood assignment of player attributes by minimizing cross-source divergence, enforcing temporal precedence constraints to ensure official transactional updates supersede stale open-data observations.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal inference to assign non-conformity scores to conflicting roster facts. By treating official league transactions as high-weight priors and open data as noisy likelihoods, the system calculates dynamic confidence intervals for every player attribute, flagging anomalies where empirical evidence violates established freshness bounds.
gse_mapping: In GSE, roster conflicts represent invalid state transitions within the situational Markov Decision Process. The reconciliation engine acts as a deterministic filter, projecting raw observational vectors onto the valid subspace of active rosters, ensuring downstream simulation kernels only ingest topologically consistent entity graphs.

primitives.name: Evidence-Weighted Reconciliation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Reconciliation Plan Compare official, open-data, and fallback records fact-by-fact.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F: Fact set (dimensionless), S: Source index (discrete), w_s: Evidence weight (dimensionless probability mass)
primitives.assumptions: All sources provide independent but potentially biased estimates of the ground truth roster state; official sources possess strictly higher reliability weights.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when source weights sum to zero or when contradictory official records yield an unsolvable constraint satisfaction problem.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's multi-sensor fusion kernel, aligning disparate data streams into a unified belief state.

primitives.name: Temporal Precedence Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Official current evidence wins unless stale or contradicted by newer official transaction evidence.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: Timestamp (ISO 8601), E_official: Official evidence vector, \tau: Staleness threshold (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Time flows monotonically; official transaction logs are append-only and cryptographically verifiable against spoofed timestamps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during network partition events where clock skew causes newer official evidence to appear temporally prior to older snapshots.

layer2.mapping: Functions as the causal ordering mechanism in GSE state transitions, preventing retroactive corruption of historical game states.

primitives.name: Immutable Snapshot Hashing
primitives.verbatim_quote: Store raw source snapshots with timestamp, URL, hash, parsed record count, parser version, and evidence IDs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H: Cryptographic hash digest (SHA-256), N: Parsed record count (integer), V: Parser version string
primitives.assumptions: Raw ingestion payloads remain immutable post-hashing; cryptographic collisions are statistically negligible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Compromised if upstream providers silently alter historical URLs without changing content hashes, breaking provenance chains.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's audit trail primitives, providing exact reproducibility for any generated player surface or rating.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by defining the roster state as a high-dimensional vector space where each dimension corresponds to a specific player attribute (team, number, status). We introduce a set of stochastic observation operators corresponding to different data sources (official, open-data, fallback). The core mathematical challenge is resolving the non-commutative nature of these updates when they arrive out of order or contain contradictions. By applying a Bayesian filtering approach, we treat the official NFL transaction log as the primary transition matrix, while other sources act as noisy measurement updates. The 'read-only' constraint implies we are performing inference on a static snapshot of this dynamic system, calculating the posterior probability of the true state given the observed evidence. The reconciliation operator effectively minimizes a weighted least-squares error function between the observed facts and the inferred truth, subject to hard constraints imposed by the temporal precedence gate. If an official update exists at time t_1, it mathematically zeroes out the probability mass of any contradictory state from t_0 < t_1. This creates a rigorous, auditable lineage for every fact presented in Player Lab or GSE Rating, transforming messy, overlapping web scrapes into a clean, provably consistent tensor of roster truth.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to distributed systems consensus algorithms like Raft and Paxos, adapted for semi-structured data. It borrows heavily from Kalman filtering used in tracking physics, replacing physical motion models with administrative transaction rules. Historically, it evolves from early sports database normalization efforts, moving from simple majority voting to sophisticated, authority-weighted temporal logic to handle the chaotic reality of live roster moves.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agents as adversarial web scrapers, lazy data entry clerks at secondary sites, and the inherent entropy of human error. The system assumes these actors will inevitably produce stale or contradictory information. By anticipating that open-data sources might lag behind official transactions by hours or days, the reconciliation engine preemptively down-weights their influence. It treats the 'truth' not as a static fact, but as a moving target that requires constant vigilance and probabilistic calibration to track accurately.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the reconciliation process attempts to mutate the production database directly. The read-only boundary acts as an anti-collinearity check, ensuring that our inference layer does not accidentally become a write path, which would break auditability. Furthermore, if the confidence interval of a reconciled fact exceeds a predefined uncertainty threshold, the system must veto rendering that fact as 'confirmed' on public surfaces, forcing a fallback to a qualified or unknown state to preserve customer trust.
